Yantis Shocks USAC Regulars At Plaza Park

By Richie Murray
November 24, 2026
0
192
Share
Facebook
Twitter
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 9:10
    Instaread

    VISALIA, Calif. — Despite entering just his fifth career USAC NOS Energy Drink Midget National Championship start on Monday night at Visalia, California’s Plaza Park Raceway, Jett Yantis counted himself to be one of the favorites to get the win.

    As it turned out, he was the clear-cut favorite.

    The confident and talented 16-year-old from Bakersfield, California took over the lead on lap two before pacing the final 39 circuits of the 40-lap Good Earth Farms Special Presented by Peelz, then successfully fended off the challenge from Kevin Thomas Jr. on the final lap to prevail in the closest USAC National Midget finish of the year by a little more than a car length, 0.203 seconds ahead.

    For Yantis, Plaza Park’s 1/5-mile dirt oval is a home away from home. He was the Non-Wing Outlaw Micro Sprint champ there in 2025 as well as the Winged Outlaw Micro Sprint titlist in both 2025 and 2026. This year, with he USAC Avanti Western States Midgets, he made two Plaza Park starts and won both. He kept his undefeated 2026 midget run at the track fully intact.

    “It’s unreal,” Yantis reflected after piloting the Beilman Motorsports/Dave.com – Smart Machine Tool – Josh Ford Motorsports – Inland Rigging/Spike/Stanton SR-11x to victory lane. “Oh, dude. I wouldn’t have wanted to win anywhere else other than Bakersfield, of course.”

    Yantis also pulled off the rare feat of winning his first career USAC National Midget feature at a track that was also hosting its first ever USAC National Midget event. The last driver to accomplish the feat was Corey Day at Indianapolis, Indiana’s Circle City Raceway in 2021.

    Furthermore, Yantis became the fourth different first-time USAC National Midget winner in 2026, following Karter Sarff, Briggs Danner, and Jakeb Boxell. Just two days earlier, Yantis had recorded his best career USAC National Midget finish to date with an impressive 10th to 2nd charge at California’s Merced Speedway.

    To top it off, Yantis also provided Kyle Beilman his first career USAC National Midget win as a car owner. Back in July of this year, Yantis also gave Beilman his first ever USAC Western States Midget victory. Beilman has fielded cars in USAC competition for the past decade, dating back to 2017.

    T.J. Smith, a four-time micro sprint champion and 49-time winner at Plaza Park, led the opening lap of the main event from the pole position. However, second starting Yantis flexed his muscle early by ripping around the outside of Smith in turn four to lead lap two by a wheel.

    Moments later, Smith’s bid for the win came to an abrupt end when he stopped in turn one at the start of lap three while running second. Smith was relegated to the tail of the field and made his way back to 14th place in the finishing order.

    Jett Barnes, the 2026 Chili Bowl Nationals Rookie of the Year who was making his USAC National Midget debut, got upside down in turn four on lap seven of the event. He was able to climb out and walk away.

    Through the middle portion of the race, Yantis drew his lead to more than two full seconds but endured a wall of traffic that surrounded his very being. That allowed the surging Cannon McIntosh to come alive once he got by Justin Grant for the second spot with a swift low line move in turns three and four on the 17th lap.

    For the next several laps, McIntosh pulled even with Yantis and was even able to surge ahead at moments. That said, each time, Yantis found a way to keep McIntosh at bay and maintain his grip of the lead. But a lap 22 yellow flag for a spin and stop by 13th running Hayden Wise resulting in lapped traffic being removed from the equation for the time being.

    The man who took full advantage of this new development was Kevin Thomas Jr. First he drove by Corey Day on the lap 21 restart for fourth. He then took Grant for third on lap 25. Up front, with 10 laps remaining, McIntosh was draped all over Yantis for the lead. There, in a turn four close call, McIntosh dinked the infield berm which sent him straight towards Yantis, resulting in the two drivers touching wheels, but continuing on without harm, nor foul.

    On lap 33, stationed two car lengths behind Yantis for the lead, McIntosh locked horns with 24th running Broedy Graham in turn two as McIntosh attempted to put him a lap down. The resulting contact between McIntosh’s right rear tire and Graham’s left rear sent McIntosh into a 360 degree spin before stopping on the back straight. McIntosh’s run for victory ended right then and there, but he did restart and finish 15th.

    Jakeb Boxell (8th) became the second driver to get upside down during the event when he flipped in turn two on lap 37 but was able to climb out and walk away. That promptly set up, in essence, a four-lap trophy dash between Yantis and Thomas for the win.

    With Thomas gaining ground on the low line, Yantis had held serve with his diamond line from the top of turn three to the middle of turn four. While there might’ve been an urging for Yantis to occupy the space on the bottom, Yantis had no inkling of doing that.

    “I didn’t really have a car set up to run the bottom,” Yantis explained. “I tried to run it a couple times down there and it slowed me down more than anything. I just decided to stick to my own line, and because I knew that if I diamonded it off, they couldn’t really get by me unless I left it or if I blew it over in turn two.”

    As Yantis held about a car length and a half lead over Thomas at the exit of turns two and four down the stretch, Yantis felt he nearly gave it away on the final lap as his car sort of straightened out and pushed on him off the final set of corners.

    “KTJ kept me honest the whole time, and on that last corner, I got tight up top and I thought it was over,” Yantis revealed. “But we were able to muscle it to the win. This car was so good all race.”

    It was over, and in a grand manner, Yantis had tallied a monumental score at Plaza Park over runner-up Kevin Thomas Jr., with Justin Grant third. Kyle Larson advanced 15th to 4th while Corey Day rounded out the top five.
